children: Shares of Victoria's Secret sank Thursday after the lingerie retailer reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings, but the company's business turnaround took a hit as sales missed expectations.

Victoria's Secret posted adjusted earnings of 95 cents a share in the fiscal second quarter ended Aug. 1, up from 33 cents a year ago and above Wall Street's expectation of 77 cents. Net sales grew 10% to $1.61 billion, slightly missing the analyst consensus call for $1.62 billion, according to FactSet.

The company also modestly raised its fiscal-year sales expectations, matching Wall Street expectations at the midpoint. The lingerie retailer's fiscal third-quarter sales guidance came in slightly above the analyst consensus.
Against heightened expectations, however, Victoria's Secret earnings and guidance weren't enough for Wall Street.

Victoria's Secret stock dropped 18% to $69.80 in premarket trading on Thursday after ending Wednesday up 0.8%. Shares had advanced 57% on the year as of the closing bell on Wednesday as investors have been impressed with the business turnaround under CEO Hillary Super.
